assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, insulinotropic activity of the truncated peptide) led to drugs that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with additional cardiovascular and renal benefit. Scientific originality and very large clinical impact are both clear.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (receptor biology, GLP-1 actions on gut and islet, translational advocacy) and Mojsov (identification of the active truncated peptide) are the most defensible academic trio. Knudsen's industrial medicinal chemistry is important but fits less well in a three-person limit; other early contributors (for example Habener) are not in the supplied credit list and credit remains contested.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and approved, widely used therapies; timing is ripe and arguably pressing given the scale of impact.
uncertainties: Priority dispute around Mojsov and others over identification of the active peptide.
Whether the prize should reward discovery biology or drug development, which could require a different configuration.
Long-term safety and durability data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patient T cells with chimeric antigen receptors created a new class of living drug with durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies; a conceptual and clinical breakthrough in cancer immunology.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CAR design with costimulation) and June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T) are the strongest pair. Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy and gene-transfer work is foundational but arguably distinct from CAR design; Eshhar is not in the supplied credit list. The third slot is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and a decade of long-term follow-up confirm efficacy in hematologic cancers; recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Attribution of the original CAR concept versus clinical development.
Limited success in solid tumours and toxicity concerns.
Whether Rosenberg's contribution is part of the same discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided a general method to control genetically defined cells with light, transforming causal neuroscience and creating a major experimental toolkit across systems neuroscience, with early clinical applications emerging.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) plus neuronal implementation (Deisseroth, Boyden, Miesenboeck) form a difficult credit problem; with six credited names and a three-person limit, any configuration excludes people with strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Widely used and independently validated for over a decade; therapeutic maturity is modest but the tool's scientific impact is established.
uncertainties: Severe allocation problem among six credited people.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signalling (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing, ATF6) and underlies understanding of proteostasis in disease, with therapeutic efforts under way.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are a clean two-person configuration; Walter established the pathway logic and IRE1 mechanism, Mori the transcriptional response and ATF6 arm. Contributions to the PERK/eIF2 arm (for example Ron) are not in the supplied credit list, a possible gap.
assessment.maturity: Mature, extensively confirmed basic biology in yeast and mammals; clinical translation still emerging, but the basic discovery is stable.
uncertainties: Other contributors (the PERK branch) are not in the credit list.
Clinical impact is indirect so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-guided antisense correction of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, the first effective disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, and validated splice-switching oligonucleotides as a platform.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO target identification) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and development) form a coherent pair; other contributors may have played roles but are not in the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term clinical experience and independent confirmation; recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Other contributors with notable roles are omitted.
Whether recognition should focus on basic splicing mechanism or the therapeutic platform.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Stem-cell-derived self-organising intestinal and other adult organoids created a widely used system for studying tissue renewal, disease and personalised medicine.
assessment.attribution: Clevers's identification of Lgr5 stem cells and the organoid culture breakthrough are decisive; Sato carried out the key culture work. A clean pair, though earlier pluripotent-stem-cell organoid work by others also matters.
assessment.maturity: Broad, independent adoption across many labs; clinical applications still developing.
uncertainties: Relationship to pluripotent-stem-cell organoid work and to earlier stem-cell recognition.
Direct medical impact is still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR as a central regulator of cell growth and nutrient sensing connects metabolism to growth, ageing, cancer and immunosuppression, with extensive therapeutic implications.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically and is the central figure; Sabatini (mammalian mTOR and nutrient sensing) and Schreiber (rapamycin-FKBP12 chemistry) have strong claims, but others in yeast and mammalian identification make allocation difficult.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and deeply confirmed; therapeutic relevance well established.
uncertainties: Credit sharing between the yeast genetics and mammalian discovery.
Whether the chemistry and mammalian arms belong to the same recognised discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cancer can arise through blocked cell death, founding the field of apoptosis regulation by the BCL-2 family and enabling venetoclax.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the cloning and family work; Vaux showed BCL-2 as a cell-death inhibitor and Strasser contributed to the family's biology. Other early contributors are not in the supplied list; the three-person limit is tight.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with approved targeted therapy and extensive independent confirmation; follows earlier apoptosis recognition but is a distinct advance.
